We first heard about Chicago Canine Academy from our neighbor, who brings her dog there for boarding, and after hearing so many great things, we decided to try training for Rizzo.

Before training, walking him was honestly so difficult. I’m pretty petite and Rizzo is an almost 80 lb American Bully, so he would basically pull me around the block the entire time. Walks were stressful instead of enjoyable.

At our first consultation, Jim was already able to get Rizzo listening, following commands, going over benches, sitting on a stool for “place,” and doing things we honestly didn’t think he would do that quickly. After seeing that, we knew we wanted to sign him up for bootcamp.

The first week of bootcamp was no visitation at all, which was definitely hard because we missed our baby so much, but we understood that he needed that time to focus and adjust. Starting the second week, we tried to go almost every day so WE could learn too. That was honestly one of my favorite parts of the entire program. It wasn’t just “drop your dog off, pick him up a few weeks later, good luck.” They actually had us come in, showed us everything Rizzo had learned, corrected us when needed, and taught us how to improve our own handling and communication with him.

I really appreciated that because training the dog is only half of it. If we didn’t understand what commands he learned, how to reinforce them, or what we should be doing differently at home, it wouldn’t have been nearly as helpful.

We were definitely sad dropping him off, but we are SO thankful we did. The difference has honestly been night and day. I feel so much more comfortable and confident walking him now, and taking him around the block is actually enjoyable instead of me getting dragged everywhere. We’re still working on a couple things, of course, but his progress has been incredible.

I also absolutely love the group training sessions. They bring us into different controlled environments, and Jim, Alges, and Diane are always nearby helping guide us, showing us different approaches, and teaching us how to get better responses from our dogs. I love that the learning continues even after bootcamp is over.

We’ve had such an incredible experience overall and are so grateful for everything they’ve done for Rizzo and for us.

Another huge bonus is that they also have raw dog food available for purchase. We’ve started using it for both of our dogs, and it has been such an easy and convenient addition to their diets.

Honestly, such a great experience for both the dog AND the owners. We’re so happy we chose Chicago Canine Academy!

This business consistently uses mine and my neighbors porch and property without the owners consent. This has cause multiple people that join these classes to just use my porch to train their dog. It’s frankly really weird to just use a strangers porch to train your dog. Please train the humans first on basic manners. It also incredibly dangerous as we are currently in the process of restoring our front porch and have had chemicals sitting out on our porch multiple times.
If you love your pup here here. WARNING you must love your pup! I have spoken!

My partner and came to Jim after my two pit mixes got into a fight with each other. It was a very stressful and emotional time, but the moment I called and met with Jim, I knew this training was going to be different than any other training we had tried. Both went through the 2 week bootcamp. Jim encouraged us to come during that time as well to work with them, and man, what a difference. We needed the training just as much as they did.

It's a different type of training than what I've had ever done. BUT IT WORKS IF YOU WORK.

8 months later, we are still going to the weekly Saturday sessions, and I never would have imagined the amount of progress both the dogs and us have made. It's the highlight of our week, being part of a community that just gets it.

And anytime we need boarding, we now have a safe place the dogs can go and I have complete faith knowing they are getting taken care of.

Jim, Algis and Diane and the whole team are pretty much the dog's (and our) favorite people on the planet now.

I cannot believe this place is still open. It has been 6 years since I brought my dog, Uno, here, and I still carry the guilt and heartbreak from that decision. Like any loving pet owner, I thought I was doing something good for him. I trusted this facility to help make our lives better, but it turned into one of the worst experiences either of us has ever gone through.

What happened to Uno during his training is something I will never forget. No dog should be treated the way he was. The methods used here were cruel, and I truly believe fear and abuse were used to force obedience. Watching the effects it had on my dog was devastating.

I trusted Jim and his Son with a member of my family, and I deeply regret it. If you love your dog and want them to be safe, please think carefully before bringing them here. I would never want another owner or another dog to go through what Uno and I experienced.

I never worry about "my kids" . I am able to relax knowing they are in great hands. I also feed my husky the Leo dog food that I purchase there. She loves the raw chicken mixes. I changed her diet and it was a mistake. She is much happier on their food. She was grumpy and irritable when I took her off of it. I am very happy with the services I receive there and will always be a customer.  I highly recommend them.

Bringing my puppy Anniken here has been the best decision. Their number one focus is the safety of your dog. They enforce this with a respect based training, which does include corrections. Seeing this from the outside vs being there and going through the training is truly night and day.
The day before I dropped her off for bootcamp I read some of the reviews and was second guessing this decision.
Going to see her on the second week was like seeing a completely different puppy, I was amazed and knew we made the right decision for her.
In the 4 months that we have been going here after bootcamp I've met a lot of dogs and dog owners. I have witnessed so much love, praise, respect, and success.
I love my dog. If that means I have to give her a few corrections to make sure she is not put into a deadly situation, that's exactly what I'll do.
I'd also like to note that choke (slip) collars, pronged collars and electric collars exist and are used/sold for a reason. The military, police, and even service dog use these collars for training some of the best dogs. It works.
If you're against the use of these, this isn't the place for you.
I will continue to bring my dog here until they get sick of us and tell us to go away.
